transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. I'm here because... well, I just can't seem to keep myself together lately. 

Ever since my daughter left for basic training, I feel like I come home to a dead house. It's really starting to affect my day-to-day life. I'm a sheet metal worker, and I find myself just sitting in the truck crying before my shifts. Once I'm actually on the floor, I'm missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years, and I've been snapping at the younger guys on the crew. 

Even when I'm off the clock, I've stopped going out on the water or working on my metal sculpture at home. I just... I just don’t see the point right now. I need some help getting back on track.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It’s been about a month. She left for basic training four weeks ago, and... yeah, I’ve been struggling like this pretty much ever since then.
Have you had any thoughts of killing yourself or not wanting to be alive?
No, no, I haven't had any thoughts like that. I mean, I'm miserable, and I cry a lot, but I don't want to die. I just want to figure out how to get through this without falling apart.
Since your daughter left, have you noticed any change in your sleep?

Not really, no. I mean... I still sleep about the same as I always have. Working on my feet all day, I usually crash pretty hard once I actually get into bed. So, yeah, I haven't noticed any real changes with my sleep. It's mostly just when I'm awake that I'm a mess.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite since your daughter left?
No, my appetite is pretty much the same. I mean, doing sheet metal work all day takes a lot out of you, so I still get hungry. I'm eating my normal meals... so, no, no real changes there either.
Since your daughter left, have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty?

No, I haven't felt like that. I don't feel worthless, and I don't feel guilty. I mean, I know I did a good job raising her, so there's no guilt there. It's just... I'm just really struggling with her actually being gone and the house being so empty. But no, I don't have those kinds of feelings about myself.
Before your daughter left for basic training, had you already been feeling depressed or losing interest in your usual activities?

No, not at all. I was managing just fine before she shipped out. Everything was normal. All of this... it really just started within a few weeks of her leaving for basic training. Before that, I was my usual self.
